raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, so I don’t make fancy plans. I look at what my land did before, what I can afford, and what other people around here are doing. This year I will still keep wheat and maize as the main thing, because that is the steady money and grain. Cotton I will keep on a smaller piece because it takes a lot of picking work, but if the price is decent it still brings cash. Chili I won’t plant too much, because it needs close watching and more labor, but keeping a small area is good in case the price is better than grain. I have a well, so if it turns dry I can save the crop, but pumping water costs money, so I won’t water carelessly.

For wheat, I do mostly the same as usual, because changing too much at my age is risky. I put decent fertilizer under it, not too little, because if wheat turns yellow later it is hard to recover. After wheat comes off, I hurry to put in maize right away on the same land. That turnaround is always tight, so I keep tillage simple. Cotton and chili I manage more carefully but on less land, because they take more hand work and my family only has so many hands. I would rather spread things out a bit than put all the land into one crop and get hurt if one market or one weather problem goes bad.
